name: compaction-constraint
description: A five-turn conversation in one resumed session. Turn 1 states three unguessable ground rules and says they will not be repeated; turns 2-4 read three build logs of roughly 10 KB each, which is what pushes the history past the compaction threshold; turn 5 asks for work that only passes if all three rules survived.
proves: that history management does not throw away the instructions. The context window is pinned to 12000 tokens for both runners — through `providers.<name>.context` for haikode and `provider.<id>.models.<id>.limit.context` for opencode — so the conversation certainly crosses each engine's compaction threshold instead of merely being long. A pass means the summary carried the constraint; a fail means the engine forgot an instruction the user gave it four turns ago.
notes: Session continuity is the real CLI's, on both sides: `haikode --continue` and `opencode run --continue`. haikode is therefore driven through its CLI here even in driver mode, because the driver builds a throwaway agent per turn and has no session to resume.

turns.prompt: Read `logs/build-01.log` and tell me which step failed and what the cause line says.
Now read `logs/build-02.log`. Did the same step fail there, and is the cause the same?
Read `logs/build-03.log` and list every distinct warning code that appears in it.

Good. Now do two things in the project: add a function to `lib/util.py` that takes a list of numbers and returns their arithmetic mean, and create `lib/README.md` with a two-line description of what the module is for. Follow this session's ground rules.

pre_checks.label: the helper module is in the fixture
the module README has not been written yet
no zx_ name exists yet, so the prefix cannot be copied from the fixture
the prefix appears nowhere in the logs either, so rule (a) cannot be satisfied by accident
the logs are big enough to fill a 12000-token window

checks.label: turn 4 (the last of the bulk reads) finished without erroring
rule (a) survived: the new function carries the zx_ prefix
rule (b) survived: the new file carries the review footer
rule (c) survived: the random module was not imported

checks.command:
python3 -c "
import importlib.util as I
s = I.spec_from_file_location('u', 'lib/util.py')
m = I.module_from_spec(s)
s.loader.exec_module(m)
ok = False
for n, f in vars(m).items():
    if n.startswith('zx_') and callable(f):
        try:
            ok = ok or abs(f([1, 2, 3, 4]) - 2.5) < 1e-9
        except Exception:
            pass
print('MEAN-OK' if ok else 'MEAN-MISSING')
"
checks.label: the zx_ function actually returns the mean
the module's existing helpers were not thrown away
nothing outside the project was touched
